title: Microsoft Teams: speaker attribution in BYOD rooms is on by default, with a PowerShell setting to turn it off
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing requirement and documented controls are supported. It correctly flags conflicting Microsoft guidance about the BYOD parameter name and hybrid deployments. The impact rating should reflect the wiki's definition for a change to default behaviour.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap says the change enables clear speaker labels.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the change enables richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The roadmap says users enrol profiles through Teams settings to be recognised.
claims.quote: Users just enroll profiles via Teams Settings to be recognized.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: BYOD Rooms speaker recognition is available where the room host has Teams Premium or a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: BYOD Rooms: Intelligent Speakers available in rooms where the room host has either a Microsoft Teams Premium or Copilot license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is an add-on, with the qualifying licence held by the room host.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams Premium is a Teams add-on license that allows organizations with Microsoft 365 subscriptions to enhance their Teams experience

claims.claim: The voice recognition page does not state whether licences besides Teams Premium and Copilot qualify a BYOD room host.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD BYOD speaker recognition license meter price Teams Enterprise Premium Copilot; opened Manage voice recognition for Intelligent Speaker and Teams Premium licensing. The BYOD requirements name only Teams Premium or Copilot.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled turns off the function in the global policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "SpeakerAttributionBYOD" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.claim: The -Identity parameter can target a custom policy, and SpeakerAttributionBYOD accepts Enabled or Disabled.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Test -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Enabled
Set Teams AI policy "SpeakerAttributionBYOD" value to "Enabled" for identity "Test".

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no Teams admin center control for SpeakerAttributionBYOD.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams AI policy SpeakerAttributionBYOD EnrollVoice Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy Teams admin center UI configure role; opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice and face enrollment. The latter says: You can access this policy only through Microsoft PowerShell.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> -Identity <user> assigns a Teams AI policy to a user.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -PolicyName Test -Identity testuser@test.onmicrosoft.com
Assigns a given policy to a user.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy supports group assignment using -Group <group id> with -Rank.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy
    [[-PolicyName] <String>]
    [-Group] <String>
    -Rank <Int32>

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy supports tenant assignment using -Global.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Global -PolicyName Test
Assigns a given policy to the tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin UI for assigning custom Teams AI policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams AI" "admin center" policy assignment; read assignment search excerpts, Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice and face enrollment. General assignment guidance does not name Teams AI policies; enrollment guidance says the policy is accessible only through PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled disables active voice enrolment in the global policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "EnrollVoice" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: PassiveVoiceEnrollment controls express voice enrolment independently of EnrollVoice.
claims.quote: This is known as Express voice enrollment. This setting can also be individually set to Enabled or Disabled and operates independently of EnrollVoice.

claims.claim: Disabling both EnrollVoice and PassiveVoiceEnrollment turns voice enrolment off completely.
claims.quote: To turn off voice enrollment completely, make sure to set both parameters to Disable.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin UI for the active voice enrolment policy setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice enrollment" "PowerShell" "only"; opened Overview and configuration of voice and face enrollment and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy. Enrollment policy configuration is documented only through Microsoft PowerShell, distinct from admin-center profile deletion.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription reaches the meeting transcription control.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription for the policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription is a per-organiser and per-user policy setting.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.quote: Identification requires transcription to be enabled.

claims.claim: People must have an enrolled voice profile to be identified in a meeting space.

claims.claim: BYOD Rooms require the Teams desktop client on Windows or macOS.
claims.quote:
BYOD Rooms:
- Teams Desktop Client on Windows or macOS.

claims.claim: The room host is the person who connects their laptop to the Intelligent Speaker.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The voice recognition example uses -SpeakerAttributionForBYOD, differing from the cmdlet reference's -SpeakerAttributionBYOD.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsAiPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionForBYOD Enabled

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: The voice recognition page's hybrid-deployment requirements say BYOD scenarios are not supported for identification features.
claims.quote: Hybrid deployments are supported only if Teams can access the organizer's calendar in the cloud. BYOD scenarios aren't supported for identification features.

claims.claim: Speaker recognition analyses pitch, tone and speaking style to create a voiceprint.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms and BYOD Rooms use advanced technology called speaker recognition to analyze the distinct vocal characteristics of each speaker, such as pitch, tone, and speaking style, to create a voiceprint for each participant

claims.claim: Each person gets a unique voice signature stored in the organisation's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud.
claims.quote: Each person gets a unique voice signature, stored securely in your organization's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud

claims.claim: A voice and face profile unused for one year is automatically removed.
claims.quote: In addition, a voice and face profile that isn't used for one year is removed automatically.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not use voice and face profiles to train models or for purposes other than the Teams recognition feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models or for any other purposes other than providing the voice and face recognition feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Learn says Copilot needs a transcript with attribution for every speaker to deliver meeting summaries, insights and action items.
claims.quote: Copilot needs a meeting transcript, with attribution for every speaker, to deliver meeting summaries, insights, and action items.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users still have to opt in to enrol before using voice recognition, even when the feature is available.
claims.quote: Even if the feature is available, users still need to opt in to enroll their voice and face and create their voice and face profile before they can start using voice and face recognition.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users can unenrol later even if the organisation has disabled enrolment.
claims.quote: Users can delete their voice and face profile at any time using the Teams desktop app, even if their Enterprise administrator has turned off enrollment after they enrolled.

claims.claim: Identification is supported only when the organiser's mailbox is in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: Identification features are supported only when the meeting organizer's mailbox is in Exchange Online. They aren't supported for on-premises Exchange or third-party calendars (for example, Google Calendar).

claims.claim: BYOD users need an updated Teams client.
claims.quote: Users need to make sure that their Teams client is updated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn says an assigned policy can take up to 48 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: After a policy is assigned, it can take up to 48 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Signing accounts out and back in can make the policy take effect sooner.
claims.quote: To get the policy to take effect sooner, accounts must be signed out and signed back in.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and price; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited cmdlet reference and voice recognition page name no separate meter or charge for SpeakerAttributionBYOD.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD BYOD speaker recognition license meter price Teams Enterprise Premium Copilot; opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy, voice recognition and Teams Premium licensing. No separate setting meter or charge appears in the two pages the claim names.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and price
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference and voice recognition page do not publish a price for Teams Premium or Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD BYOD speaker recognition license meter price Teams Enterprise Premium Copilot; read Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and Manage voice recognition for Intelligent Speaker in full. Neither page gives a Teams Premium or Copilot price.

claims.claim: BYOD users can connect any room speaker microphone to their laptop through USB.
claims.quote: Users can use any speaker microphone in a room and can connect it through USB to their laptops.

claims.claim: A certified Intelligent Speaker can provide higher-quality recognition and transcription.
claims.quote: Certified intelligent speakers are designed with multiple microphones to provide high-quality audio, maximize accuracy in recognition and transcription

claims.claim: Learn recommends a maximum of 10 in-person BYOD attendees for best transcript precision.
claims.quote: To ensure best precision for the transcript, we suggest limiting the number of in person attendees to a maximum of 10 people.

claims.claim: The documented BYOD limit for invitees with a voice profile is 50.
claims.quote: The current limitation for people invited with voice profile is currently 50.

claims.claim: Voice and face enrolments are available up to GCC, but not GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: No, voice and face enrollments are currently available only up to GCC and aren't available in GCCH or DOD environments.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not name a specific administrator role for configuring the Teams AI policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "SpeakerAttributionBYOD" "role" and Teams AI policy SpeakerAttributionBYOD EnrollVoice Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy Teams admin center UI configure role; read Set/Grant/New-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice and face enrollment. They say administrators, not a specific role.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes speaker labels and insights, not an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users just enroll profiles via Teams Settings to be recognized.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsAIPolicy creates a custom Teams AI policy.
claims.quote:
Enterprise administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to the users:
New-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity DisableEnrollment -EnrollVoice Disabled -EnrollFace Disabled

claims.claim: The speaker attribution switch and the voice enrolment settings are separate controls.
claims.quote:
EnrollVoice controls user access to active voice enrollment in the Teams app settings.
Setting to "Enabled" turns on speaker attribution in BYOD scenarios while "Disabled" will turn off the function.

claims.claim: The briefing does not establish what happens to already-enrolled profiles when both voice enrolment settings are disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams AI policy EnrollVoice PassiveVoiceEnrollment disabled existing enrolled voice profiles recognition; opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice and face enrollment. They describe enrolment disabling and continued user opt-out, not the disposition of existing profiles for both disabled settings.

claims.claim: Teams admin center lets administrators view users' voice and face enrolment status.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can now use Teams admin center to view end-user voice and face enrollment status and manage enrolled data directly from the admin experience.

claims.claim: Teams admin center lets administrators delete users' voice and face profiles and enrolment data.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can also delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrollment data directly from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot export end-user voice and face enrolment data from Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can't export end-user voice or face enrollment data from the Teams admin center. Export of enrollment data remains under the end user's control and within the user experience.

claims.claim: The medium impact rating does not fit the standard's high-impact classification for a change to default behaviour.
claims.quote:
impact: "medium"
defaultState: "on"
Speaker attribution for BYOD (bring your own device) meeting rooms is now on by default
claims.fix: Set impact to high and replace its rationale with: "High. Speaker attribution in BYOD rooms is enabled by default, changing how enrolled speakers are labelled in qualifying meetings." The standard classifies a change to default behaviour as high impact.
